reason: A turns the request into a tight eight-step game: you draw your own week (step 3), the reveal locks your guess and puts your miss next to the copy's 1,561 MW and the 163-of-168-hours overshoot (step 4), then Chronos-2's 980 MW and 37% cut is added (step 5), and the 'This week / All 20 forecasts' toggle (step 6) shows AutoARIMA's 0.58 becoming 1.11. That sequence gives the 'feel' the request asked for, and every screen fits a 390 px phone without clipping. B is the more complete and careful piece: it adds the interval undercoverage (65.5-70.1%), the 'order not a finding' and 'lead over AutoETS not established' caveats, a per-series heatmap and clickable per-method forecasts. But at phone width it has visible faults: the axis labels overlap in section 4, the heatmap hides the USD/CAD and AI page-view columns (the point of section 5) behind a horizontal scroll, and the first chart opens with its MW axis scrolled off-screen. B also lets you keep adjusting your guess after the actual week is shown, which weakens the guess-then-reveal test. A's polish and pacing narrowly outweigh B's extra depth.

A: Never shows the aggregate result that the pretrained models' 80% ranges held the actual value only 65.5-70.1% of the time; step 5 shows only this week's 140/168 band, which makes the intervals look better than the study found.
Step 6 'This week' view sorts rows by the 20-forecast average, so TimesFM 2.5 (0.37) and AutoARIMA (0.58) sit mid-list; the caption below does not change when you toggle to 'All 20 forecasts'.
The 8 step dots wrap onto two rows at 390 px, and steps 1-5 leave a large empty gap between the chart and the text.
B: Section 4 chart: the '1.00 = copy last week' label overlaps the 0.5 and 1.5 tick labels into unreadable text at phone width.

Section 5 heatmap is wider than the card at 390 px, so the USD/CAD and AI page-view columns, where 'last week still wins', are hidden until the reader scrolls the table sideways; the first chart also opens with its MW y-axis scrolled off-screen, and the section 3 chart ticks are tiny.

After the reveal the slider and drawing stay live ('Keep adjusting'), so readers can fit their line to the visible actuals; the untouched default, a tie at 1,561 MW, is reported as 'Last week beat you'.
